## Example 5.1 {#ss5-example-5-1 .gp-lesson}

a) Write down the first term $a$ and the common ratio $r$ for each of the following geometric sequences:

::: {.gp-subparts}
i) $2,\ 4,\ 8,\ 16,\ldots$

ii) $3,\ 1,\ \dfrac13,\ \dfrac19,\ldots$

iii) $\sqrt3,\ \sqrt6,\ \sqrt{12},\ldots$
:::

b) Suggest how the common ratio could be found when given any two successive terms.

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 28 · Example 5.1</p>

::: notes

(a)(i) a=2,r=2. (ii) a=3,r=1/3. (iii) a=√3,r=√2, since √6/√3=√2 and √12/√6=√2. (b) Divide the later term by the immediately preceding term: r=a_n/a_(n−1). Do not invert the ratio. Keep working in the booklet or OneNote.

:::
